host.note: Reconstructed session: the replies were written by an agent playing this session; every embed was computed by the host from the graphs named.

turns.request: Put the analytics values into a copy of duplex-base.ifc as property sets.
turns.reply: 2,469 values on 228 entities. The table below holds 2,441 of them, on 224 entities, grouped by property set: 872 NRC_OperationalCarbon, 868 NRC_EmbodiedCarbon, 654 NRC_EnergyPerformance, 28 NRC_StoreySummary, 12 NRC_AnalyticsProvenance, 7 NRC_BuildingSummary. I did not call Run in this session; this notebook must not write files, and the `answer` node still shows EffectPending above. `samples/nrc/duplex-enriched.ifc`, already committed to the repository, is the output of an earlier Run of this same graph (workflow 6's write-back). Here it is beside the base file: duplex-base.ifc is 2,380,763 bytes (sha256 b347a2c8…606ed), duplex-enriched.ifc is 2,709,099 bytes (sha256 c263e08c…8600078), 328,336 bytes larger.

Not from this session's tools: that needs an entity-level IFC diff, which no graph in this notebook computes. `tests/flow/BimOpenFlow.NrcWorkflows.Tests/RollupGraphTests.cs` runs one: `Enriched_DiffersFromTheBaseOnlyByTheAddedSets` asserts zero deleted and zero changed entities between the two files, and exactly 663 new IFCPROPERTYSET, 663 new IFCRELDEFINESBYPROPERTIES, and 2,469 new IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE entities — the 2,441 rows of the first table plus the 28 zone values — along with the four IfcZone groups, their four IfcRelAssignsToGroup, and the long table's document reference. `EnrichRun_WritesTheCommittedFileByteForByte` runs a fresh Run and asserts its output matches the committed file byte for byte. I hashed both files myself instead of repeating that test (previous turn); a plain byte-prefix comparison would not prove it, because the appended entities land before the STEP file's closing lines, not after its last byte.
